source_read: PMC HTML, PMC3380537 (author manuscript): abstract, all sections, Tables 1 to 3 as text, figure legends, footnotes 1 to 5, acknowledgments, author information, reference list; read in full before the card was opened. Figures 1 to 3: figure image not viewable (screenshot of my tab came back blank), values not extracted. No claims in the task (card check only).

key_findings.note: The same paragraphs also say how the interaction results changed under each definition; see missed item 1.
All 16 onset interaction terms in Table 3 have intervals including 1.
Every number matches Table 3; all recurrence intervals include 1.

Wording only: 16.7 to 17.3 is the range in the four groups with dependence at Wave 1 (persistent, recurrent, offset, non-recurrent); the new-onset group also has present dependence, so 'the groups with past or present dependence' is ambiguous. Men: 65.4 to 72.4%, so '65-72%' is right.

reporting_issues.note: The issue is right: 0.02 and 0.03 are three-way interaction terms. The point estimates are right (0.22 x 4.56 x 9.56 x 0.02 = 0.19; 0.84 x 2.14 x 1.90 x 0.03 = 0.10). Two corrections. (1) Rounding range: about 0.14 to 0.25 (not 0.24) for parenthood and 0.08 (not 0.09) to 0.12 for a new job. (2) The consequence 'about ten times weaker' holds only for parenthood (0.19 vs 0.02, 9.6 times). For a new job, 0.10 vs 0.03 is about 3.4 times.

Under the same coding, the parenthood-persistence point estimates by cell are: women 21-37, 0.22; men 21-37, about 1.00; women 38+, about 2.10; men 38+, about 0.19 (editors' arithmetic; no intervals). The association changes direction across cells, which supports the consequence.

Checked against the Table 2 subscripts: married W1 persistence 34.3a = offset 35.3a; married W2 persistence 37.7a = onset 41.5a = offset 42.2a; parent W2 offset 51.0a = persistence 52.8a = onset 55.2ab.
With 6 df, age entered as seven categories, so this is an omnibus test.
The reference list title of Crum et al. (2005) begins 'Incidence rates for alcohol dependence among adults', which supports checking the unit.
The reference list has Research Triangle Institute, SUDAAN Version 9.0, 2004; the Method says version 10.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E is high overall, driven by confounding, for the life-transition associations. The descriptive decomposition is reasonably separated in the reasoning. I agree with the domain judgments.

interpretation_gap.note: 'Minor' is defensible because the abstract hedges ('tended to', 'not dramatically') and the decomposition headline follows from the results. However, the Results misread the interaction terms by a large factor. Any claim on parenthood or employment and persistence must use the card's reporting issues 0 to 1, not the paper's text.

missed: Robustness of the persistence three-way interactions differs by check. With multiple imputation, only the parenthood interaction stayed significant (Results > Role Transitions..., 3rd paragraph). With persistence redefined as AD at Wave 1 plus at least one symptom at Wave 2, only the job three-way interaction was significant (Results > Alternative Definitions of Persistence and Recurrence, 1st paragraph). With a continuous-diagnosis definition, only the parenthood interaction remained (2nd paragraph). Neither interaction survives every check; key findings 5 and 7 should say so.

New onset and recurrence count only dependence present in the 12 months before Wave 2. Dependence that began or recurred and then remitted earlier in the roughly three-year interval is not counted, so it falls into the 'consistent non-diagnosis' or 'non-recurrent' groups. The 2.5% and 8.8% in key finding 4 are therefore past-year statuses at follow-up among the people at risk, not three-year cumulative incidences, and they understate onsets and recurrences over the interval. The authors call their approach 'time-sampling' (Results > Alternative Definitions..., 2nd paragraph).
